assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's strontium implementation, turned atomic spectroscopy into a roughly 10^-18 instrument. The idea is conceptually clean and the realisation is demanding. The impact reaches the redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants. As an atomic physicist I value both the many-body-limited systematic-error control and the elegance of the magic-wavelength concept.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice and led early Sr clocks. Ye's group brought the clock to the lowest systematic uncertainty and drove the many-body and collective-shift physics. Both credited names are central, and a two-person prize is natural. Other groups are not credited here, so the pairing is coherent but not exhaustive.
assessment.maturity: Very mature. Many independent laboratories have reproduced the clocks, international comparisons are routine and the roadmap to redefine the SI second is in progress. The timing is good, because the technology is established and no longer speculative.
uncertainties: Recognition may be seen as overlapping with the 2005 and 2012 prizes on frequency combs and ion control, so its novelty relative to them has to be argued.
Credit may also be claimed by ion-clock and other lattice-clock groups outside the two credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller 1995 proposal showed how to compute with laser-cooled trapped ions, using motional-mode gates and individual addressing. It defined a physical architecture for quantum computing that later experiments realised. Its scientific originality is high, and it builds directly on the quantum-optics toolbox that earlier prizes recognised only in part.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the clear theory originators. Blatt's group made decisive early demonstrations of the gate and then of scalable ion-trap processors. Other experimental groups share the experimental credit, so the experimental third slot is somewhat arbitrary. Choosing Blatt follows the supplied credited names.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a proposal and as an implementation, with several laboratories and commercial devices. The wider field of quantum computing is still evolving, so a prize would honour the foundations rather than a finished technology.
uncertainties: Which experimentalist best represents the demonstration is disputed, and the earlier prize for ion control partly covers the experimental ground.
The same theorists appear in other packages (B045, B027, B017), so a consistent decision about how Cirac and Zoller are recognised is needed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted flat bands at magic twist angles. Jarillo-Herrero's group then found correlated insulators and superconductivity in 2018. This opened moire quantum materials as a tunable platform for correlated physics, with exceptional impact across condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the quantitative prediction in 2011. Jarillo-Herrero's group performed the experimental discovery, and other groups' work was also important. Allocating experimental credit is delicate. A prediction-plus-discovery structure supports a three-person prize.
assessment.maturity: Rapid but well replicated across many groups. The mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene is still debated, so a longer maturation period might be natural. The structural discovery is firmer than the mechanism.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity remains unsettled.
Results on related moire systems by other groups complicate the division of credit.
Whether the prize is premature relative to better-established topics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kane-Mele prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators established a new classification of band insulators. Molenkamp's HgTe experiment confirmed the edge channels. The concept has changed how materials are classified and has led to a large body of follow-up work. It is important and conceptually deep, although outside my own specialist area.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele are the decisive theorists. Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental realisation, building on the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. The BHZ authors are not in the supplied names, which complicates the full record of credit. The supplied three-name set is workable.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with extensive confirmation through ARPES and transport in many materials, and the topological classification program has been consolidated for over a decade.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe prediction (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) is not included in the supplied names.
Overlap with B025, which combines Kane and Mele with Xue, means the configuration needs a single consistent choice.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED brought cavity-QED strong coupling into superconducting circuits. It enabled dispersive readout and the architecture that underlies most superconducting quantum processors. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, so this candidate is related but addresses a distinct step: controlled light-matter interaction with artificial atoms.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf and Wallraff wrote and demonstrated the 2004 proposal and strong coupling. Four names are credited, so at most three can be chosen, and omitting Blais is a real loss on the theory side. Related transmon work lies outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the sense of broad adoption and replication across many laboratories, though the larger quantum-computing application is still developing. Closeness in time to the 2025 prize could argue for waiting.
uncertainties: The 2025 prize on superconducting circuits may reduce appetite for a nearby topic.
Dropping Blais or Girvin leaves a theory-credit gap, and the transmon contributors lie outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical-lattice quantum simulation realised the Hubbard model with cold atoms, including the superfluid-to-Mott transition and quantum gas microscopy with single-site resolution. It created a new way to study many-body physics with controllable parameters. Importance is high and the platform is widely used.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and Cirac) proposed the Hubbard-model realisation. Greiner and Bloch did the Mott-insulator experiment and led quantum gas microscopy. Five names are credited, so a choice of three necessarily leaves out Dalibard and Cirac, which makes the configuration contested.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature. The experiments have been confirmed on many platforms, and the major landmarks date from 2002 onward. The long-term scientific payoff is still emerging, particularly for fermionic and spin-resolved simulations.
uncertainties: Substantial overlap with B015, B045 and B017 in the Zoller and Cirac credit.
Credit among Bloch, Greiner, Dalibard and Cirac is contested, and the earlier BEC prize is adjacent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Aharonov-Bohm effect and Berry's geometric phase show that gauge potentials and parameter-space geometry carry physical consequences. These concepts underlie modern topological physics, molecular dynamics and quantum computing. Conceptual clarity and breadth of impact are very high, and geometric phases are used routinely in atomic and molecular physics.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov and Bohm published in 1959, but Bohm died in 1992 and cannot be recognised. Berry's 1984 phase had antecedents such as Pancharatnam's work. The two-person configuration is workable but historically incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Extremely mature and experimentally confirmed many times over, with foundations established decades ago. Recognition would be overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: A prize on the Aharonov-Bohm effect would exclude Bohm and Ehrenberg-Siday, a delicate historical point.
Predecessors such as Pancharatnam complicate originality claims for the Berry phase.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Production and control of ultracold molecules extend laser cooling to species with rich internal structure. This enables precision tests of fundamental symmetries such as the electron EDM, ultracold chemistry and new quantum-information platforms. The concept is significant, and the underlying molecular spectroscopy and structure physics are attractive.
assessment.attribution: Doyle and DeMille pioneered buffer-gas cooling and laser cooling of molecules, and Ye's group contributed molecular and precision work. Other groups (for example those assembling KRb molecules) are not in the credited names, so credit allocation is open.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature. Laser cooling and trapping of molecules is reproduced across several groups, but the key applications (EDM limits, chemistry, quantum simulation) are still developing, so recognition is somewhat early.
uncertainties: There is no single clear decisive discovery spanning association and direct laser-cooling lines of work.
Ye also appears in B051, so honouring the same person for two topics would be awkward.
